summary: This RFC specifies a network model for attachment circuits, usable to provision them before or during service provisioning such as VPNs or network slices. It has a companion service model.

eli5.summary: It is the provider's own view of the customer links, used when setting up services.

questions: what is the ietf-ac-ntw yang module
ac network model vs ac service model
how are attachment circuits modeled on provider edge
subtitle: The provider-side YANG model that records how each attachment circuit is built on its Provider Edge nodes.

tldr.problem: A customer-facing AC service model hides which provider nodes terminate an attachment circuit, but the network controller needs a place to store and manage those node-level details.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-ac-ntw YANG module augments the generic ietf-network model and the Service Attachment Point (SAP) model with per-node AC data: Layer 2 and IP connection details, routing, OAM, security and service parameters, plus a reference back to the service-layer AC.
tldr.outcome: Controllers can provision and track ACs on PEs before or during service delivery (VPNs, RFC 9543 Network Slice Services) and correlate them with the customer's AC service request.

today: RFC 9835 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2025. It has not been obsoleted or updated. It is the network-model companion to the service models in RFC 9834.

sections.title: Why a Network Model for ACs
sections.content:
Customers connect to a provider through termination points such as Customer Edges (CEs), peer border routers, data center gateways or Internet Exchange Points. The same attachment circuit (AC) may host several services, such as L2VPN, L3VPN or an RFC 9543 Network Slice Service. To avoid service interference and duplicated information, a provider may manage ACs network-wide and let customers refer to them when ordering services. The service-level model for that is RFC 9834.

This RFC adds the network model ietf-ac-ntw. It manages the PE side of ACs inside the provider network. It reuses the AC provisioning structure of the L3VPN and L2VPN network models (RFC 9182 and RFC 9291) and refines it to also cover other deployments, such as cloud networks.
sections.eli5: The customer sees a simple order form. Behind the scenes the provider needs a detailed work sheet saying which of its machines carry each order. This RFC is that work sheet.

sections.title: Where the Network Model Sits
sections.content:
The module imports ietf-ac-common (RFC 9833), the same base used by the bearer and AC service modules of RFC 9834. To correlate a customer's AC request with the AC actually provisioned, ietf-ac-ntw keeps the AC reference exposed by ietf-ac-svc. The ietf-ac-glue module of RFC 9836 augments the VPN service and network models with references to both.

In the service delivery stack, customer service models sit above service orchestration, while network models such as ietf-l2vpn-ntw, ietf-l3vpn-ntw, ietf-sap-ntw, ietf-ac-glue and ietf-ac-ntw sit between service orchestration and network orchestration. Lower down are network configuration models and device configuration models.

Like the SAP model (RFC 9408), the module can describe both User-to-Network Interface (UNI) and Network-to-Network Interface (NNI) ACs. In a provider-to-provider link, the ASBRs of one network behave as a PE and treat the neighbor's ASBRs as if they were CEs.
sections.eli5: The layers are like a company: the front desk takes orders, managers plan the work, and technicians configure machines. This model is a sheet the managers use.

sections.title: Overall Structure and Parent ACs
sections.content:
The module is built as augmentations of two existing models. It adds specific-provisioning-profiles and ac-profile lists under each network, and an ac list under each node. It also augments the SAP model so that each SAP lists the ACs it terminates. A SAP can terminate one or more ACs, and each AC can have one or more peer SAPs.

Unlike the AC service model, an AC is identified by a name within a node, not a network. Each AC stores a svc-ref to the customer-facing AC, a description, a status with administrative and operational parts (a mismatch can reveal an anomaly), and group membership for redundancy or protection.

When one AC has several peer SAPs (for example two CEs) but some need specific data, an operator can define a Parent AC that lists all CEs and create Child ACs bound to it with parent-ref. Children inherit the parent's properties. Whenever a Parent AC is deleted, all its Child ACs MUST be deleted. Profiles work the same way: values in an ac-profile are inherited unless refined at the AC level, where the AC-level value takes precedence.
sections.eli5: A parent AC is like a family recipe, and child ACs are versions of it for each guest, such as one without nuts. Throw out the family recipe and all its versions go too.

sections.title: Profiles and References
sections.content:
The module defines groupings for referencing an AC on a specific node in a given network, an AC profile, and each kind of specific provisioning profile. This follows the design of the generic network model (RFC 8345).

As in RFC 9182 and RFC 9291, the exact definition of provisioning profiles is local to each provider. The model only carries identifiers so local policies can be bound when an AC is built. The identifiers are for encryption, QoS, failure detection (for example BFD policies), forwarding (for example ACLs) and routing (for example BGP policies).

An ac-profile has a name that is unique in a network and can hold routing protocol parameters (BGP peer groups, OSPF, IS-IS, RIP, VRRP) and BFD settings under OAM. Some nodes can be adjusted at node level, and adjusted values win over the profile.
sections.eli5: Profiles are like saved settings you can reuse on many links. The model just stores the names, and each provider decides what the names mean.

sections.title: Layer 2, IP and Routing Details
sections.content:
The l2-connection container manages the PE side of the Layer 2 setup. It covers encapsulation (dot1q, priority-tagged, QinQ) with tag operations such as pop, push and translate, Layer 2 tunnel services (pseudowire, VPLS, VXLAN), a l2-termination-point for implementations that need a sub-interface, a local-bridge-reference, the bearer-reference and LAG interface details.

The ip-connection container groups IP addressing for IPv4, IPv6 or both. It supports three address assignment modes for customer addresses: provider DHCP, DHCP relay and static addressing. For IPv6, SLAAC can be used. In the RFC's example, a local-address of 2001:db8:0:1::1 with a prefix-length of 64 gives the prefix 2001:db8:0:1::/64. During transitions such as network merging, two ACs with overlapping information may be kept and correlated by the same svc-ref.

The routing-protocols container supports static routes, BGP, OSPF, IS-IS, RIP and VRRP. The oam container holds failure detection such as BFD, security specifies encryption for the AC traffic (direct Layer 2 or Layer 3 encryption, or a local encryption profile), and service carries the MTU, bandwidth (inbound and outbound, using rates such as CIR, EIR and PIR), QoS and ACL profiles.
sections.eli5: This part fills in the details of one link: how its packets are labeled, which addresses it uses, how routes are shared, and how big and fast it may be.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is accessed through YANG-based protocols such as NETCONF and RESTCONF, which have to use secure transport and mutual authentication. NACM (RFC 8341) can limit what users may do.

Writable data is sensitive. Someone who can change ac data could alter QoS, bandwidth, routing protocols or keying material and cause SLA violations, or add a new AC. Changes to specific-provisioning-profiles, which are tagged nacm:default-deny-write, could manipulate routing, QoS or encryption policies.

Readable data is also sensitive. It can reveal a customer's peer-sap-id, and the Layer 2 and Layer 3 connection details can be used to track a customer. The keys in keying-material and customer-key-chain could be used to inject spoofed routing advertisements. As in RFC 9834, keys are given as ASCII strings, because a hexadecimal format is not supported by the underlying device modules.
sections.eli5: The work sheet has the real details and secret keys of every link. Only the right people should be able to read or change it, or they could mess up or spy on customers' connections.
